subrounds.goal: Locality inputs: boundary decay of the AM2 creation coefficients and boundary independence of the finite-volume dynamics (F1 versus F2), both from admitted constants.

loops.title: Weighted creation norm and boundary decay of the AM2 coefficients
loops.direction: paired (forward: Steiner-star weighted norm, Lemma W, and a boundary-weighted Lipschitz argument; reverse: complex-coupling analyticity, Cauchy estimate and tree locality)
loops.target: (T1) For every F1 and F2 box, every onsite cutoff and every 1 ≤ w ≤ 1/(37888|tau|) (390625/148 at |tau|=10^-8): ||c||_{sigma,w} ≤ 1/64, with sigma(M) the least number of overlap-connected star translates covering M. (T2) For u in R={0,e_z}: sum_{M ni u} ||c^{N'}_M - c^{N}_M|| ≤ (1/32)(37888|tau|)^{n_0}/(1-37888|tau|), with n_0=N for F1-F1 and F2-F2 (N'≥N+1≥2) and n_0=N-1 for F1 against F2 on the same box; preview at the cap and N=2: 4.49e-9. Mandatory label: coefficient decay, not convergence of states. Retained failure: only cardinality weights close (limited: smallness in support size, no distance decay).

loops.title: Boundary independence of the dynamics on compact time windows and existence of the F2 dynamics
loops.direction: paired (forward: polynomial F(r)=(1+r)^-4; reverse: exponential F_lambda(r)=e^{-lambda r}(1+r)^-4 with lambda=1)
loops.target: For A in B(H_R), ||A||≤1, |tau|≤10^-8 and common clock theta=alpha t/hbar: sup_{|theta|≤1} ||tau^{F2,N}_theta(A)-tau^{F1,N}_theta(A)|| ≤ 3969 tau^2 e^{127008|tau|} (5N+1)/N^3 (at most 5.5e-13 at N=2 at the cap), using C=224, ||Phi||_F≤2268|tau| and the 28N(5N+1) extra faces at l1 distance at least N-1; and the F2 box evolutions converge in norm, uniformly on compact windows, to the AQ1 automorphism group T_theta. Retained failure: the interaction-picture Lieb-Robinson form does not apply to the face commutator (limited, no F2 dynamics).

subrounds.reason: Both loops are most feasible: BA2 uses only admitted constants (AQ1, AY2 face count) and a Duhamel identity; BA1 needs one short lemma on top of the AM2 majorant. They are independent and supply the inputs of BB1 (weighted norm for route A; exponential Lieb-Robinson constants for route B).

subrounds.goal: Whole-sequence convergence of the R-marginal with an explicit rate, a common limit omega_inf for F1 and F2, and the correlation functions, gap and translation invariance of that limit.

loops.title: Whole-sequence convergence of the R-marginal, common limit of F1 and F2, explicit rate
loops.direction: paired (forward route A: hard-core polymer gas of pairs (F,F') from psi(s)=e^{-C(s)}Omega_0, Kotecky-Preiss with evaluated weights, uniform bound K, Cauchy estimate in the complex coupling; reverse route B: AM2 gap along the interpolation H(theta), exponential Lieb-Robinson, imaginary-time clustering and static susceptibility)
loops.target: Exact rationals C and q below 1 with ||rho^{Fi,N}_R - rho^{Fj,N'}_R||_1 ≤ C q^{N-1} for all N'≥N≥2 and i,j in {1,2}. Tiers: (a) some q below 1 (whole-sequence convergence and a common limit; every subsequential limit of either family equals omega_inf on R); (b) q≤1/1000 and C≤4 at |tau|=10^-8 (route A candidate q=222/390625, K≤2); (c) ||rho^{F2,5}_R - rho^inf_R||_1 ≤ 2K_2' tau^2 (about 2.68e-12). Required wording: whole-sequence convergence of the named constructions, not uniqueness of infinite-volume ground states. Retained failure: KP not closable with evaluated constants (forward limited: coefficient decay only); C_B not explicit (reverse limited). A failed route is not evidence that limits differ.

loops.title: Correlation functions, gap and translation invariance of the limit
loops.target: For bounded local A on R and |theta|≤1: |c^{Fi,N}_A(theta) - c^inf_A(theta)| ≤ an explicit bound decaying exponentially in N (via a Lieb-Robinson ball approximation and the BB1 rate on the ball); omega_inf composed with any coarse translation equals omega_inf; the AQ2 gap alpha/16 and vacuum simplicity hold in the GNS representation of omega_inf. Retained failure: only polynomial-F rates close (limited: O(1/N)).

subrounds.reason: BB1 is the central new mathematics (a standard method with a large margin at the cap: KP sum at most 1/32 against a=1/10) and settles the literal roadmap goal 1 for the named families plus AY2 obligations O2, O4 (and O3 via BB2). BB2 is assembly once BA2 and BB1 are admitted.

loops.title: Uniqueness beyond the named constructions: boundary-class tier and obligations statement
loops.target: Certified tier: the same limit omega_inf arises from every bounded boundary interaction satisfying AM2 hypotheses H1-H5 with J≤J_0 (route A covers these verbatim). Statement: the missing premise between this and uniqueness among all infinite-volume ground states (omega(A*[H,A])≥0), with the Yarotsky-type local-gap route, an updated six-row obligations table and a falsifying scenario. Target note: feasibility and format check for the statement; blind threshold only for the boundary-class tier.

applications.problem: Gauge-group transfer of the link-flip lemma (U(1), Z2, SU(N), U(N), Sp, SO; SU(3) with center Z3)
applications.equation: U_E H(tau,kappa) U_E^* = H(-tau,-kappa), with E meeting every plaquette oddly and U_E left multiplication by a central z on the links of E
applications.expected_outcome: Holds iff some central z acts as -1 in the Wilson-loop representation: SU(2k), U(N), U(1), Z2, Sp(2k), SO(2k) vector. Fails for SU(N) with N odd, SO(2k+1), G2 and adjoint loops. For SU(3), multiplication by omega=e^{2 pi i/3} maps Re Tr U_f/3 to Re(omega^{+-1} Tr U_f)/3, a flux-twisted Hamiltonian, not a sign flip; only the Z3 N-ality selection rule and charge conjugation survive.
applications.assistant_computation: Enumerate centers and representation phases; verify pi-flux flip sets E={x-links, y even} on Z^2 boxes and E={x-links, y+z even} union {y-links, z even} on Z^3 boxes and on the 24-link factors; exact moment tables.

applications.problem: Center-grading first-order parity (AW1) for other groups
applications.equation: First-order terms of omega(W^2), C(s), c(theta) vanish by single-occurrence orthogonality and E_Haar[W^3]=0
applications.expected_outcome: Holds iff E[W^3]=0: every SU(N) with N not 3 (including SU(5), where the flip lemma fails), U(N), U(1), Z2. Fails for SU(3) (E[W^3]=1/108 with W=Re Tr U/3; preview E[(Re Tr U)^n]=1,0,1/2,1/4,3/4), G2 and SO(3); the SU(3) obstruction is a certified nonzero first-order centered coefficient proportional to E[W^3].
applications.assistant_computation: Exact Weyl-integration moments for SU(2..5) with python-flint fmpq; exact first-order centered coefficient on an SU(3) one-plaquette graph.

boundary_decay.verdict: feasible: coefficient decay is nearly immediate from AM2 (complex coupling or Steiner-star weights, same constant); state decay needs a standard Kotecky-Preiss polymer expansion with a large margin at the cap
boundary_decay.candidate_rate: Coefficients: sum_{M ni u}||c^{N'}_M - c^N_M|| ≤ (1/32)(37888|tau|)^N/(1-37888|tau|) (ratio 148/390625 = 3.7888e-4 at the cap). States (route A): ||rho^{F1,N}_R - rho^{F1,N'}_R||_1 ≤ 2K q^N/(1-q), with exponent N-1 when F2 is involved, q = 56832|tau| (222/390625 = 5.68e-4 at the cap), candidate K≤2; previews 7.3e-10 at N=4 and 4.2e-13 at N=5. Route B: C_B |tau| N^{5/2} e^{-mu_B(N-1)}, mu_B about 0.841 at the cap, C_B of order 10^2-10^3.
obstacles: The AM2 contraction is in an unweighted sup-type norm; distance-to-R weights are the wrong object (the bulk fixed point is translation covariant) and cardinality weights do not control extent (M contains N minus X, so supports thin out); Steiner-star weights or complex-coupling analyticity are needed.

The R-marginal depends on the normalized outside state (AV1 normalization trap); a recursive shell argument gives t^k (k!)^3-type products and no convergence proof; a polymer (KP) expansion of ⟨psi(sbar),psi(s)⟩ with evaluated weights and a uniform bound K is required.
The reach count n_0 (N or N-1) must be verified exactly for both families, including partial F2 stars.
Route B: NS06 clustering assumes finite-dimensional sites; the imaginary-time step must be redone for unbounded commuting Casimir terms in the interaction picture.
The rate is in N at fixed tau and fixed spacing; nothing is uniform in a; uniqueness among all infinite-volume ground states is not implied.

dynamics.verdict: feasible and essentially mechanical with the admitted AQ1 constants
dynamics.candidate_bound: ||tau^{F2,N}_theta(A) - tau^{F1,N}_theta(A)|| ≤ (|tau|/336) [(e^{kappa|u|}-1-kappa|u|)/kappa] sum_{f,x,y} F(d(x,y)) ≤ 3969 tau^2 theta^2 e^{127008|tau||theta|} (5N+1)/N^3 ||A|| with u=theta/8, kappa=1016064|tau|, F(r)=(1+r)^-4 (O(N^-2)); with F_lambda multiply by e^{2 lambda} e^{-lambda(N-1)} and replace kappa by kappa e^{2 lambda} (exponential in N). Same-family Cauchy rate: O(1/N) with polynomial F, O(e^{-lambda N}) with F_lambda.
obstacles: The interaction-picture Lieb-Robinson bound (NS14 form, unbounded commuting onsite terms) must be checked for the commutator with a bounded face W_f exactly as written.
The polynomial F gives only polynomial decay; the exponential F_lambda is admissible because the interactions are finite range but its constants must be re-evaluated.
Correlation-function consequences need the BB1 state rate on balls growing with N.

dissents: The per-chain-step factor is J G(R)/R = 37888|tau| (about 3.79e-4 at the cap), set by the ball condition; J G(R) below 1/64 is an absolute smallness statement, J G'(R) = 9856|tau| is the fixed-point Lipschitz constant and 2J G'(R) is the excited-sector constant. None of the latter three should be pre-registered as a rate.

Coefficient decay does not give convergence of states: the R-marginal depends on the global normalized outside state. Coefficient decay (BA1) and state convergence (BB1) should be separate loops with separate labels.
The weighted norm should weight support extent (Steiner star count), not distance to R; distance weights belong on the difference between two boxes, measured from the boundary.

Roadmap goal 1 in its literal wording (any two subsequential limits of the named families agree on R) is subsumed by BB1; the word uniqueness should be reserved for the strong form (all infinite-volume ground states), which stays open and goes to BC2.
The expected O(N^-2) Duhamel rate holds for F1 against F2 on the same box; the same-family Cauchy rate with F(r)=(1+r)^-4 is only O(1/N). Do not pre-register N^-2 for the Cauchy step.

The 10^-8 cap has a factor of about 2600 of slack in the AM2 contraction itself (the inequalities hold up to |tau| about 2.6e-5 with the frozen J=28|tau|), and for the uniform model it is partly a blocking artifact (site blocking gives a candidate cap near 5.27e-4). This changes no continuum conclusion but should be recorded before any contract re-freezes J_0.
closing: This lens admits nothing and counts zero research loops.
